Title: Police cripple armed gang linked to 17 luxury house break-ins in Sabah
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah police have crippled an armed syndicate linked to 17 gang robbery and luxury house-breaking cases involving RM304,500 in losses across several districts since early this year, said Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun.
He said the breakthrough was achieved through two special operations, Op Casa and Op Pintu, following the formation of a special task force in September to investigate two armed robberies reported in the state capital in August.
Six men, aged between 30 and 43 with a combined 75 criminal and drug-related records, were detained, while police have launched a manhunt for several other suspects still at large.
"Police also seized various valuables, including luxury watches, designer handbags, electronic devices, cars, fishing equipment, and a safe box.
"The syndicate targeted unoccupied luxury residences and did not hesitate to use bladed weapons to intimidate victims if anyone was inside," he said in a statement today.
Jauteh said investigation papers have been completed and all suspects are scheduled to be charged at the Kota Kinabalu magistrate's court tomorrow.
They will face charges under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code for armed gang robbery, and Section 457 of the same code for house-breaking.
The suspects also face charges under Sections 411 and 414 of the Penal Code for retaining and disposing of stolen property, Section 447 for criminal trespass, and Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
"Police remain committed to taking continuous action against any individual or group involved in criminal activities to ensure the peace and well-being of the community, especially in Sabah, are safeguarded," he said.

Title: 130 Malaysians arrested in Pakistan scam centre raid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakistani authorities arrested 130 Malaysians in a raid on an online scam centre in Rawalpindi.
Pakistan news portal ProPakistani reported that the scam centre targeted Malaysians.
It said the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) raided the premises at KASA Tower, Bahria Town Phase VIII, after obtaining a court warrant.
Digital devices and equipment seized during the raid indicated that the premises was being used to carry out financial scams targeting Malaysians.
The suspects allegedly contacted victims through internet-based calling applications, posing as bank customer service officers and claiming that suspicious or unauthorised transactions had been detected in their accounts.
Victims were then transferred to people posing as Malaysian police officers, some of whom allegedly wore police uniforms and used office-like backgrounds during video calls.
They then threatened victims with money laundering accusations, criminal charges and legal action before pressuring them to transfer money.
The proceeds were reportedly received through eWallet transactions before being converted into cryptocurrency through various channels.
Investigations found that the syndicate was allegedly run by a Malaysian operating from Cambodia, with supervisors and call centre managers overseeing operations in Pakistan.
A Chinese citizen suspected of receiving cryptocurrency from the syndicate and converting it into Pakistani rupees was also identified during the investigation.
ProPakistani reported that Pakistani authorities listed all 130 people, including their passport details, in a police report.
All those detained were Malaysians, according to the report.
Some were also found to have overstayed their visas or were suspected of being in Pakistan without valid immigration documents.
However, their immigration status and the extent of each individual's involvement remain subject to further investigation.
The case is being investigated under Sections 13, 14 and 16 of Pakistan's Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 as well as relevant provisions of the Pakistan Penal Code relating to extortion, impersonation, fraud and abetment.
The authorities are continuing to investigate the alleged overseas organisers, local supervisors and individuals involved in handling the financial transactions.
The total losses suffered by victims, the number of confirmed victims and the value of money seized have yet to be disclosed.

Title: Youth Parliament elections set for Nov 1-2
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,689 candidates from 12 parties will contest 222 seats nationwide in the Malaysia Youth Parliament (PBMy) elections on Nov 1 and 2.
Dewan Rakyat speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said the elections would use a proportional representation system, with voting conducted online via the ePBMy application.
Johari, who is also PBMy patron, said the approach would expose young people to an alternative system of representation while leveraging digital technology to facilitate participation in the democratic process.
"I urge all Malaysian youths aged between 18 and 30 who registered as voters through the ePBMy application by Oct 28, 2026, to participate in the voting process on Nov 1 and 2," he said in a statement today.
He said the elections were part of ongoing efforts to strengthen young people's understanding of and appreciation for parliamentary democracy.
Johari said the participation of 1,689 candidates reflected youths' interest and willingness to engage actively in the democratic process and contribute ideas and views on issues affecting the country's future.
He said PBMy was not merely a contest to elect youth representatives, but also a platform for democratic education, providing first-hand exposure to elections, representation systems, policy debates and leadership responsibilities.
"Through this experience, I hope young people will understand that democracy is not just about winning elections, but also requires maturity, integrity, mutual respect and a willingness to accept differing views."
Johari said PBMy should remain a non-partisan platform for democratic education, free from the influence of mainstream political parties and open to youths from diverse backgrounds.
He expressed hope that the initiative would nurture a future generation of leaders who were knowledgeable, principled and mindful of their responsibilities to society and the nation.

Title: Budi Madani a success in targeted subsidies, curbing leakages - Amir Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Budi Madani programme has been described as one of the country's successes in implementing targeted subsidies that not only help ease the people's cost-of-living burden but also curb fuel subsidy leakages.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said that under the Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) programme, eligible Malaysians can purchase RON95 petrol at RM1.99 per litre compared with the unsubsidised price of RM4.42 per litre, with a monthly quota of up to 300 litres.
He said Malaysians could also enjoy subsidised diesel at RM2.10 per litre compared with the unsubsidised price of RM5.27 per litre, with a monthly quota of up to 400 litres.
"Budi Madani is one of the country's successes. This is one of the methods we have introduced to reduce the people's cost-of-living burden, while increasing their disposable income.
"For example, motorists who use 100 litres of RON95 petrol a month can enjoy savings, while those who use the full 300-litre quota will benefit from even greater savings," he said.
He said this when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 (2027 Budget) at the policy stage for his ministry in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Meanwhile, Amir Hamzah said using MyKad as a verification mechanism for eligibility to purchase subsidised petrol had helped curb leakages, particularly purchases by foreigners who are not eligible for the subsidy.
He said the savings generated by efforts to reduce leakages could be channelled back into improving assistance for the people and strengthening the country's fiscal position.
He said the government had also taken action against those involved in subsidy misappropriation, including a recent case in Nibong Tebal.
Commenting on a proposal to exclude the top 20 per cent (T20) income group from receiving RON95 subsidy, Amir Hamzah said the matter needed deeper consideration, as the government did not want to place additional pressure on the people.
"For now, our efforts are to reduce the people's burden and not put them under further pressure. The issue is to ensure we curb the leakages that are occurring. That is where we can achieve the savings we want," he added.

Title: Appeals Court set aside Bolivian's guilty plea on drug trafficking charge, remits for trial
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal has set aside a Bolivian's plea of guilt on a charge of trafficking in 3.714kg of cocaine and remitted his case to the High Court for trial.
Rafael Nunez Pax had been convicted and sentenced to 30 years' imprisonment by the High Court in 2025 after he pleaded guilty to the charge.
Yesterday, a three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, allowed Pax's appeal on grounds of justice.
Delivering the court's decision, Justice Noorin said the court was of the view that the strict guidelines governing Section 173 of the Criminal Procedure Code laid down by Court of Appeal judge Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan in the Teh Geok Chin v PP case had not been strictly complied with, particularly whether Pax understood the consequences of his plea.
She said the range of punishment must be explained to the appellant (Pax), and it must be put on record by the judge.
"Because of that, we are allowing the appeal. We remit this matter to the High Court for trial," Justice Noorin said.
Paz's lawyer, Hasnan Hamzah, assisted by Qushwa Hasnan, argued that his client's lack of understanding of the procedures at the High Court stage meant his guilty plea was conditional.
"Therefore, it was unsafe for the High Court judge to convict Paz of an offence under Section 39B (1) (a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952," he said.
He said Paz, in his affidavit, stated that he was merely following the advice given by his lawyer at the time and believed he would be given the opportunity to explain his side of the story to the court after the plea.
He said in the grounds of judgment, the High Court judge only indicated that Paz, a taxi driver, understood what was conveyed by the Spanish interpreter, but did not explain or elaborate on the nature of that understanding.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Aqilah Syaza Ariffin argued that throughout the proceedings in the High Court, a Spanish interpreter was present to translate on behalf of the Pax, and the charge was also read out in Spanish.
According to the charge, Paz was accused of committing the offence at the passenger screening branch, Level 3, Domestic Arrival Hall, KLIA 1 Terminal, Kuala Lumpur International Airport, Sepang, Selangor, at 6pm on Aug 1, 2023.
On June 4, 2025, Paz pleaded guilty to the charge, and the High Court convicted him and sentenced him to 30 years in jal, beginning from the date of his arrest on Aug 1, 2023.

Title: PM: Governance, fiscal discipline key to investor confidence
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Governance and fiscal discipline remain key to strengthening investor confidence and making Malaysia a more attractive investment destination, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said sound institutions and fair rules were essential to sustaining growth amid geopolitical tensions that were shifting trade patterns.
"That is why this government has put a great deal of effort into governance and fiscal discipline, and into making Malaysia a more attractive place to invest.
"The results are showing.
"In the first half of this year, Malaysia recorded RM218.5 billion in approved investments," Anwar said in a special address at Bursa Malaysia's 50th Anniversary Gala Dinner tonight.
Malaysian companies, he said, must move up the value chain in semiconductors, advanced manufacturing and digital technology, while strengthening their competitiveness in international markets.
He also called for more mid-tier companies to expand and become regional champions, saying Bursa Malaysia had a role to play in helping promising businesses scale up.
"Too many good companies stay small for far too long.
"If it succeeds, we should see more Malaysian businesses grow, more good jobs created, and more Malaysians holding a stake in the country's growth," he said.
He also said companies seeking public investment must act honestly, while investors should be able to trust the institutions underpinning the market.
"The basic principle here is simple - a company that asks Malaysians to invest in it must deal with them honestly.
"A good business should be able to raise capital on fair terms.
"Malaysians who save and invest would be able to trust the institutions behind the market," he said.
He said Bursa Malaysia had grown from 264 listed companies and a market capitalisation of about RM12.7 billion to more than 1,100 listed companies and a market capitalisation of over RM2 trillion.
Among those present were Deputy Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan and Plantation Industries and Commodities Minister Datuk Dr Noraini Ahmad.

Title: Bersatu to field 8 candidates
Article:
MELAKA: Bersatu will field eight candidates in the upcoming 16th Melaka election.
Its vice-president, Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Jidin, said the eight state seats the party will contest are Klebang, Lendu, Gadek, Sungai Udang, Pantai Kundor, Pengkalan Batu, Ayer Keroh and Bemban.
Radzi said this at the party's candidate announcement ceremony at the Bersatu operations room in di Baitul Tariq, Klebang.
[[nid:1566500]]
Among the names that attracted attention was former Pengkalan Batu assemblyman Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee, who will try to win back the seat.
Norhizam, affectionately known as "YB Beliau", won the seat in the in the 14th state election which was held simultaneously with the 14th General Election, when he was with DAP
He stood as an independent candidate in the 2021 Melaka election.
Meanwhile, Melaka Bersatu election director Datuk Seri Mohamad Ali Mohamed will contest the Klebang seat.
He is expected to come up against Pakatan Harapan's Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir and Datuk Lim Ban Hong, who is hoping to retain the seat for Barisan Nasional.

Title: Spain train crash death toll rises to 69 as rescuers search wreckage
Article:
URDA: Rescuers picked through mangled carriages on Thursday in a grim search for victims of Spain's second fatal high-speed train crash this year, as the death toll rose to 69 and hopes of finding further survivors faded.
After cranes worked through the night to lift parts of the wreckage of Wednesday's crash, emergency workers were seen carrying what appeared to be a body wrapped in a blanket from one of the trains in the central Spanish province of Toledo.
Regional leader Emiliano Garcia-Page said the death toll had risen to 69 people and that human remains had been found during overnight rescue efforts. Work now involved crane operations, particularly on a carriage that was still overturned.
"We do not believe there could be any more fatalities beneath that one, but I say this with caution," he said.
UNIONS BLAME LACK OF FUNDING
Meanwhile, train drivers in Spain went ahead with a previously planned strike to press for more investment in railway safety a day after Europe's deadliest train accident since a 2013 derailment in Spain's Santiago de Compostela.
"We will continue demanding the necessary measures to make this sector safe again ... It must have all the safety systems required to maintain the quality standards we have always had," said Diego Martín of the train drivers' union SEMAF.
"We cannot tolerate, under any circumstances, this type of incident happening again. Everyone should be able to travel without the risk of suffering this kind of accident," he added at Madrid's Atocha railway station.
The crash, which followed another fatal accident in January involving the same rail companies on the same line, has also upended campaigning for a Nov 29 snap election, with the leaders of Spain's two main parties suspending campaign events.
Spain's government has declared three days of national mourning for those killed in the crash, which Transport Minister Oscar Puente said happened after several trains stopped due to a signal failure. A state-run Renfe train was then authorised to proceed at normal speed, even though there was a stationary Iryo-operated train ahead, Puente said on Wednesday.
Unions have already blamed a lack of funding and will to improve safety, saying that talks after the accident in January were abandoned in April. Meanwhile, the government has said that the decision to authorise the Renfe train to continue its journey was "inexplicable."
POPE SENDS CONDOLENCES
Pope Leo sent his condolences to the families of those killed, wished a speedy recovery to the injured and conveyed his support and comfort to all affected, the Vatican said, adding he had also encouraged rescue workers to continue their efforts.
Of those injured, authorities said 57 remained in hospital.
The crash prompted a major operation, which Spain's interior ministry said involved the deployment of more than 800 military and police personnel, over 200 vehicles, three helicopters, a mobile command post, drones, mounted units and search dogs.
As investigations began, a judge in Toledo barred anyone not involved in emergency, security, healthcare or judicial work from the crash site with a 2km  exclusion zone in both directions along the Madrid-Seville high-speed rail line.
Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who travelled to Toledo to take part in a meeting to monitor and coordinate the emergency response, said authorities were working "day and night" to support the victims and their families and to "get to the bottom of every last detail of this tragedy."
Meanwhile, Alberto Nuñez Feijoo, leader of the centre-right People's Party, which is currently leading in polls, was due to visit the town of Urda, where local people rushed to help with rescue efforts in the aftermath of the crash.
FOREIGN NATIONALS AMONG CASUALTIES
Spain's foreign ministry said 42 foreign citizens from seven countries were involved in the crash, information available so far showed, of whom one was killed and at least seven injured.
Wednesday's accident has added urgency to a debate about safety on Spain's railways, Europe's longest network and until recently a source of pride in the country.
Train drivers would go ahead with their strike to press for structural changes in railway safety, SEMAF said, adding that it was studying further action.
Renfe said the strike caused significant disruption to rail services, adding that passengers could change or cancel tickets free of charge and would be notified of affected services.--REUTERS

Title: Houthis report 12 killed in Saudi strike on Yemen homes
Article:
SANAA: The Iran-backed Houthis said on Thursday that a Saudi strike on a residential area in Yemen's western Taiz province killed 12 people, as casualties mount in the months since the conflict reignited.
The Houthis and the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised Yemeni government have exchanged daily attacks since a years-long truce fell apart over the summer. In recent weeks, the group has ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia.
"As an initial toll, 12 citizens were killed and three others were critically injured when the Saudi enemy targeted the homes of the families of Ibrahim Saeed Mohammed Ahmed Al-Qouz and Al-Raabi Saeed Mohammed Ahmed Al-Qouz in Al-Barah, Maqbana district," the Houthi health ministry said in a statement shared by the group's Saba news agency.
More than 1,600 people have been killed in Yemen since hostilities resumed, with more than 275,000 displaced, according to United Nations figures.
On Wednesday, at least 14 people were killed in Saudi strikes on a petrol station and market, according to the Houthis, while the group targeted the airport in government stronghold Aden, wounding civilians.
In July, a fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen's capital Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.
Later, the Houthis declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before seizing Yemen's entire Red Sea coast in a lightning campaign.
The Houthis have in turn reported frequent Saudi airstrikes.
Yemen has been reeling from war since 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital, with a Saudi-led coalition entering the conflict a year later in support of the government.--AFP

Title: Hong Kong leader apologises for Wang Fuk Court blaze that claimed 168 lives
Article:
HONG KONG: Hong Kong leader John Lee apologised on Thursday for a deadly fire that killed 168 people, and the city's housing minister resigned after a report found the government partially responsible for the disaster.
The Nov 26 fire at Wang Fuk Court was the world's deadliest residential building blaze since 1980 and engulfed several residential tower blocks.
Public pressure for government accountability has grown since then, with calls for Lee and top officials to resign.
Lee and seven other top city officials bowed and apologised at a news conference on the report concluding a months-long inquiry into the fire.
"I am deeply saddened. I would like to apologise to the affected residents and the general public," Lee said.
The city's housing minister, Winnie Ho, who resigned from her post, should "bear political responsibility", Lee added.
Four government bodies, including the fire services department, "should bear part of the responsibility for the high casualties caused by this tragic fire", the report released by authorities on Thursday said.
The Housing Bureau's Independent Checking Unit "should bear a greater share of responsibility", it added.
- 'PERFECT STORM' -
The apartment complex was a home to more than 4,600 residents, 1,700 of them over the age of 65. Of those who died, 114 people – or about 70 per cent – were aged 65 or older.
Almost all fire safety measures failed that day because of "human errors", the judge-led inquiry committee heard earlier this year.
Authorities have filed charges, including manslaughter, against seven individuals and two companies over their roles in the fire. At least 35 people have been arrested.
On Thursday, the government said regulators were "deceived" by contractors, who "are the main culprits responsible for the occurrence of the inferno and the high fatalities in the tragic incident."
The report said a number of contractors "conducted no substantive work and were only asked to lend their names to rubber-stamp statutory forms in return for a fee."
But officials said the incident was a "perfect storm" exposing the worst parts of the various regulatory regimes relating to fire safety issues concerning the city's building maintenance sites.
The November fire was the result of "the faults and deliberate misconduct of various individuals from the private sector and decades of failure" by the government and bodies responsible for construction, fire safety engineering and building management, the report said.
It said the fire "was most likely caused by a glowing source, likely a cigarette, which ignited paper materials on the flat roof outside."
The government, it added, failed to "appreciate and address the danger and the likely risk of a devastating fire when the buildings are undergoing major building maintenance renovation works."
Lee told reporters on Thursday that authorities have proposed "systematic reforms" to prevent similar incidents in the future.
They include establishing a criminal offence targeting bid-rigging, which is the "root of the problems" in building maintenance projects.
Lee said "administrative accountability" would be pursued within three months.
Prosecutors have alleged construction companies used non-flame-retardant materials to cut costs. --AFP

Title: Mayang Pasir road to remain closed until Nov 7 for sinkhole repairs
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Repairs to the sinkhole along Lebuhraya Mayang Pasir are expected to be completed by Nov 7, with the affected road remaining closed until the work is finished.
Penang Infrastructure Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the cause had been identified as damage to a 750mm concrete pipe.
"Site safety has been enhanced, and the sinkhole has been temporarily covered with a steel plate," he said in an update on the repair works.
According to Zairil, Indah Water Konsortium (IWK) is carrying out repairs in stages, including diverting water flow and pumping water out of the sinkhole.
He said sheet piling, or shoring, was scheduled to begin tomorrow morning to stabilise the surrounding soil before excavation work started.
"The overall repair works, covering the damaged pipe and road, are expected to be completed by Nov 7.
"The affected road will remain closed until repairs are completed. Motorists have been advised to use alternative routes via Lebuh Mayang Pasir, Jalan Mahsuri and Lorong Mayang Pasir 1."
Zairil apologised for the inconvenience caused and thanked road users for their patience and cooperation.
It was reported that a 2.5m-wide, 4m-deep
sinkhole
opened on Lebuhraya Mayang Pasir yesterday afternoon, forcing a road closure and emergency repair works.

Title: Malaysian chef nabbed in Mauritius over RM2.3mil cannabis smuggling attempt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 55-year-old Malaysian chef was arrested in Mauritius after suspected cannabis worth 26.88 million Mauritian rupees (RM2.3 million ) was found concealed in his luggage on Oct 23.
The man was detained at Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport after arriving on a flight from Dubai.
Mauritius news portal News Moris, quoting Defi Media, reported that police later attempted to identify the intended recipient of the drugs by replacing the seized substances with dummy packages in a sting operation.
But, the sting operation failed when nobody turned up to collect the packages.
Police also seized the suspect's mobile phone for forensic analysis, 8,150 Mauritian rupees (RM697) in cash, as well as Malaysian and Thai currencies.
The suspect remains in police custody and faces a provisional charge related to the importation of dangerous drugs for the purpose of distribution.
The arrest is the second of its kind this year involving a Malaysian in Mauritius.
On Sept 15, a 70-year-old Malaysian was arrested at the same airport after arriving from Kuala Lumpur.
Authorities seized 6.18kg of cannabis worth 9.27 million Mauritian rupees (RM793,000) from his luggage.

Title: MOH opens recruitment for 750 medical officer posts in Sabah, Sarawak
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Health Ministry (MOH) will conduct a special recruitment exercise to fill 750 permanent Medical Officer Grade UD10 vacancies in Sabah and Sarawak, with applications open from Nov 9 to 15.
MOH said the recruitment is open to all contract-appointed medical officers who began their housemanship training from Series 1/2016 on Dec 5, 2016, to Series 6/2024 on Oct 14, 2024, including those whose service contracts had expired.
"To be eligible, candidates must have successfully completed their housemanship training and obtained full registration with the Malaysian Medical Council by the closing date of the application advertisement at the latest," MOH said in a statement today.
The ministry said eligible and interested officers could submit their applications through the Public Service Commission's SPA9 system when the recruitment advertisement opened.
"For officers who are successful in securing permanent appointments, the proposed reporting date is Feb 15, 2027," the statement said.
The ministry said the recruitment exercise was part of the Madani government's commitment to making permanent appointments for more than
9,000 medical officers
, as announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling the 2027 Budget.
"This proactive measure is also designed to narrow the staffing gap and ensure that the retention of the medical workforce in Sabah and Sarawak remains at an optimal level," the statement said.

Title: Govt not considering GST return while incomes are low, living costs high
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will not consider reintroducing the Goods and Services Tax (GST) until people's incomes reach a reasonable level and the cost of living stops being a burden.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the government was, for now, focusing on improving the Sales and Service Tax (SST), taking into account the people's ability to pay, businesses' compliance costs and the capacity to generate national revenue.
"GST tends to be regressive for low-income groups, who spend a larger share of their income on goods and services," he said.
Amir Hamzah was winding up the debate on the 2027 Supply Bill in the Dewan Rakyat here.
"SST provides room for a more progressive and targeted approach, where the government can choose what to tax."
Amir Hamzah said that although part of the tax burden could be passed on to consumers through prices, the SST scope could be set with the people's ability to pay in mind.
On compliance, he said nearly 700,000 businesses, or 90 per cent, were registered under the GST in 2018, compared with only about 130,000 businesses under the SST in 2026.
"This means that under the GST system, more companies had to manage reporting and bear compliance costs compared with the existing SST system.
"As stressed by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, as long as people's incomes have not reached a reasonable level and the cost of living is still burdensome, reintroducing GST is not the government's choice."
Amir Hamzah said improvements to the SST had also raised government revenue.
According to the Fiscal Outlook 2027, SST collections rose from RM55.9 billion in 2025 to an estimated RM67 billion this year. They are projected to reach RM73.3 billion in 2027, an increase of RM17.4 billion over two years.
He said SST collections now amounted to 3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP), the same level as the GST in 2017.
"This means that proposals to replace the SST with the GST would not necessarily generate additional revenue.
"It only shifts the tax burden from the business sector, including exports, entirely to the people."

Title: No Malaysians affected by deadly Spain train collision - Wisma Putra
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: No Malaysians were affected by the deadly high-speed train collision near Urda, Toledo, Spain, on Wednesday, the Foreign Ministry confirmed.
In a statement on Thursday, the ministry thanked the Spanish authorities for their assistance and cooperation with the Malaysian Embassy in Madrid.
"The ministry wishes to also convey the appreciation of the Government of Malaysia to the relevant Spanish authorities for their valuable assistance and cooperation to the Embassy of Malaysia in Madrid in its effort to verify whether any Malaysian nationals were affected by the incident," it said.
Malaysia also extended its deepest condolences and sympathies to the Spanish government and people over the tragedy, which resulted in deaths and injuries.
Media reports stated that two passenger trains collided in Spain's Toledo province on Wednesday after a computer malfunction disabled the safety system. Authorities have said nearly 70 people had been
killed

mourning

Title: 30 foreigners detained in raid at iron ore mine in Lubok Setol
Article:
RANTAU PANJANG: Thirty foreigners were arrested during a raid at an iron ore mine in Kampung Gual Dalam, near Lubok Setol, here today.
General Operations Force Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the raid was carried out about 5am following public tip-offs about the presence of undocumented foreigners at the premises.
He said those arrested comprised 16 Bangladeshi men, 12 Indonesians men and two Indonesian women, all aged between 25 and 53.
"All the foreigners were found to have entered Malaysia without valid travel documents or overstayed," he added.
Radzi said the foreigners have been handed over to Pasir Mas police for further action.

Title: Nabil Azlan races to sim racing gold in Thailand
Article:
NABIL Azlan struck gold in the Esports Assetto Corsa category at the Asia Pacific Motorsport Championship (APMC) 2026 in Pattaya, Thailand, extending Malaysia's winning record in the discipline.
The 24-year-old dominated the competition at Bira Circuit on Saturday, winning the quarterfinals and semifinals before securing victory in the final.
The gold medal marked an improvement on his silver medal in the iRacing category at the 2025 championship.
Malaysia has now won gold in esports at every edition of APMC since the event began in 2023.
Fellow Malaysian competitor Iqbal Suji, 28, also reached the Assetto Corsa final on his championship debut, finishing sixth overall after progressing through the qualifying rounds.
However, Malaysia's campaign in the iRacing category proved less successful.
Raja Amirul Syauqat, 22, reached the final on his APMC debut but saw his medal hopes dented by a collision involving an Australian competitor.
Starting seventh on the grid, Raja was pushed to the back of the field following the incident.
Despite battling the Australian driver over several laps, he managed to recover one position to finish ninth overall.
Meanwhile, 16-year-old Ethen Low, the youngest competitor in the esports discipline, reached the iRacing semifinals before an incident ended his campaign prematurely.
Despite missing out on the final, the teenager gained valuable experience competing against some of the region's leading sim racers.
All four Malaysians secured their places in the national squad by finishing among the top two in their respective national qualifying competitions sanctioned by the Motorsports Association of Malaysia (MAM).
Representing Malaysia under MAM, the team competed against racers from more than 15 countries, supported by Esports Integrated and the Youth and Sports Ministry through the Malaysia Esports Accelerator Programme.
Hosted by the Royal Automobile Association of Thailand, APMC 2026 ran from Oct 23-25, featuring athletes from across the Asia Pacific region competing for medals in five motorsport disciplines.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesian forest fires: Report linking JCorp to incidents unfounded - Onn Hafiz
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Reports linking Johor Corporation (JCorp) to forest fires in Indonesia are false and unfounded, said Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
Onn Hafiz said no party should take advantage of the situation by distorting facts and creating the perception that the state-owned investment institution was involved in the incident.
He said all parties had the right to demand transparency and accountability, but such demands must be based on facts and credible evidence.
Onn Hafiz, who is also JCorp chairman, said the state government would continue to defend JCorp's integrity, credibility and reputation against unfounded allegations.
"Claims linking JCorp to the ownership or current operation of the companies concerned, as well as to the forest fires, are false and misleading," he said in a statement.
He said JCorp had also clarified in an official statement that companies within its group did not own or operate any plantations outside Malaysia.
He said Kulim (Malaysia) Bhd, through its subsidiary, had divested its interests in five plantation companies in Indonesia in 2007 and disposed of its entire equity interests in two other Indonesian companies on July 6, 2023.
Yesterday, JCorp issued a statement denying claims linking it to Indonesian plantation companies allegedly associated with forest and land fires, following a report published by non-governmental organisation (NGO) Wahana Lingkungan Hidup Indonesia (WALHI).
JCorp clarified that it did not own or operate any plantations outside Malaysia.
WALHI recently alleged that 21 companies linked to Malaysian business entities were allegedly involved in forest and land fires in Indonesia between January and September this year.
The findings were disclosed in a report titled 'Actor Mapping Analysis: Who Are Behind the Fires?', published by the organisation's National Executive.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget passes second reading despite uproar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget, formally known as the 2027 Supply Bill, passed its second reading by a majority voice vote in the Dewan Rakyat.
This is despite an uproar from Datuk Seri Shahidan Kassim (PN-Arau), who repeatedly interjected, arguing with Second Finance Minister Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul repeatedly pleaded with Shahidan to sit down.
It began with Shahidan trying several times to ask Amir Hamzah about EPF withdrawals, and whether the Government-Owned Entities Bill would also aim to curb an alleged "corporate mafia".
Shahidan also took a swipe at Datuk Seri Radzi Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) over the
confidence and supply agreement (CSA)
signed earlier between the government and several Bersatu MPs.
Amir Hamzah later addressed Shahidan's question, saying that the EPF's main mandate was to strengthen savings for retirement.
He said that after the Covid-19 pandemic, withdrawals totalling RM145 billion had a big impact on members' retirement savings.
Only 41 per cent of active formal members reached an adequate savings level, up from 33 per cent after the four withdrawals, he said.
Shahidan stood up again as Amir Hamzah finished, prompting Mohd Sany Hamzan (PH-Hulu Langat) to shout for him to sit down.
Johari told both of them to sit, but when Shahidan did not relent, the speaker smacked his table.
"Arau, my friend. An elder, former administrative officer, former minister, behave. The world is watching you. I'm appealing to you. Sit down. Please, Arau," he said.
Another commotion followed when Datuk Dr Ahmad Marzuk Shaary (PN-Pengkalan Chepa) rose to ask about the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on the
Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB)
sukuk.
Sany stood again and told him to sit.
As the commotion continued, Johari called for a voice vote on the Supply Bill, which passed.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tabled the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat on Oct 9.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TSH Resources finds no business links to 10 Indonesian firms named by Singapore NEA
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: TSH Resources Bhd said its review of records to date has not identified any business relationship with any of the 10 companies named by Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) regarding forest and peatland fires in Indonesia.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, the palm oil company, which operates in Malaysia and Indonesia, said none of the 10 companies is a subsidiary, associate or joint venture of the group.
"The group has not identified any shareholding in, or direct operational, supply-chain or business relationship with any of them," it said.
The NEA issued preventive measure notices to the 10 companies under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act 2014.
The companies are PT Bumi Andalas Permai, PT Bumi Mekar Hijau, PT Paramitra Mulia Langgeng, PT Sumatera Alam Anugerah, PT SBA Wood Industries, PT Hutan Lestari Raya, PT Bangkanesia, PT Buana Megatama Jaya, PT Mananjung Hayak, and PT Baratama Putra Perkasa.
TSH Resources said it received enquiries from Singapore Exchange Regulation Pte Ltd (SGX RegCo) on Oct 28, 2026, relating to matters covered by the NEA notices.
"The group is in the process of reviewing its records and compiling the documents and information requested, and will continue to engage and cooperate with NEA on the provision of such documents and information.
"The responses are based on the information available to the company and the records reviewed as at the date of this announcement, and may be updated as the review progresses. The company will make further announcements as and when there are material developments," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thailand strips rabbi of citizenship after 16 trips on US passport
Article:
BANGKOK: Thailand's government said Thursday it had revoked the citizenship of a prominent head rabbi who was a naturalised Thai, as the country tightens enforcement of its immigration laws.
Rabbi Yosef Chaim Kantor's Thai citizenship was stripped over his repeated use of his US passport after naturalisation in 2013, according to an interior ministry statement.
The order was signed by Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, who is also interior minister.
Thai law prohibits naturalised citizens from continuing to use their former nationality, although it is not always enforced.
Tourism is a major source of income for Thailand, but the behaviour and businesses of foreigners living in the Southeast Asian country has come under growing scrutiny.
Foreign nationals have been accused of using Thai proxies to circumvent restrictions on non-Thais owning land and businesses.
Kantor arrived in Thailand in 1993, according to the Jewish Association of Thailand.
After naturalisation, he continued to use his US passport up to 16 times to travel to Australia, the interior ministry said.
"Any illegal act, whatever it involves, must be dealt with firmly," Anutin told reporters on Thursday when asked about the order.
Anutin, who won February's elections on a nationalist platform, revoked Kantor's citizenship under the 1965 Nationality Act.
The move came after Thai authorities earlier this month raided three Jewish organisations in Bangkok, including Chabad House, where Kantor works.
Police said at the time that Chabad Foundation Bangkok was found to be employing three Myanmar workers without work permits.
Police also seized evidence such as tax filings and land purchase and building construction records from Gan Chabad, a Jewish school.
Chabad is an Orthodox Jewish movement headquartered in New York with venues around the world.
Rabbi Nehemya Wilhelm, of the Chabad House in Bangkok, told AFP on Thursday that the organisation legally employed about 40 workers and paid a fine for three from Myanmar whose documents had been in the midst of processing.
He said Kantor has lived in Thailand for more than 30 years, and used his US passport to visit the United States and Australia.
"Thailand is his home," said the rabbi, who also holds Thai citizenship.
"It's really painful to get such a decision just because he has another citizenship."
"We feel the tension," Wilhelm added – but "Thailand welcomes Jewish people" and "we don't feel under threat."
Kantor, who Wilhelm said was visiting New York, could not be immediately reached for comment on Thursday.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MyEG hit with RM353mil tax bill, government suit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd's wholly owned My EG Sdn Bhd (MyEG) has been slapped with RM353.13 million in additional tax assessments by the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN).
The government also filed a civil suit over the matter, according to Zetrix AI's filing with Bursa Malaysia today.
The assessments, received on Wednesday, cover transfer pricing adjustments and deemed interest, including penalties, for the years of assessment 2021 to 2023.
Zetrix AI said the assessments comprise RM333.10 million in transfer pricing adjustments and RM20.02 million in deemed interest.
The company said the same notification informed MyEG that the government initiated civil proceedings against it in connection with the tax dispute.
MyEG, however, maintained that it has strong grounds to challenge the assessments and will take the necessary steps to protect its interests, including defending its position through the appropriate legal channels.
It has also appealed against the assessments before the Special Commissioners of Income Tax while seeking an amicable resolution with LHDN.
Zetrix AI said it will update Bursa Malaysia on any material developments related to the legal proceedings.
In a separate filing, the company clarified that it had yet to receive any official letter from the government concerning a news report published two days earlier that it planned to sue Zetrix AI over RM314 million in alleged arrears.
The latest disclosure places MyEG's tax dispute under greater scrutiny with the additional assessments and civil proceedings potentially exposing the company to a substantial financial and legal liability.
Transfer pricing refers to the pricing of transactions between related companies, particularly across different tax jurisdictions.
Tax authorities may adjust such transactions if they consider the pricing inconsistent with the arm's-length principle, which requires related-party dealings to reflect terms comparable to those between independent parties.
The outcome of MyEG's appeal and the government's civil suit could determine the company's eventual tax liability.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Praise be to God': Rain brings relief to haze-hit Indonesian city
Article:
PALANGKARAYA: Residents and firefighters in an Indonesian city long shrouded in a toxic haze brought on by months of wildfires rushed outside dancing and chanting as rain this week brought a welcome respite.
Intermittent rains have been falling in Palangkaraya, the capital of Central Kalimantan province on Indonesian Borneo, where devastating wildfires have raged since August.
On Wednesday night, exhausted volunteer firefighters jumped around in the puddles and kissed the ground in gratitude as another burst came down.
"We were overjoyed; every one of us volunteers was so happy that we prostrated ourselves in gratitude. Praise be to God that there was finally rain," firefighter Lukman El Hakim told AFP.
More than 11,000 people have been treated for respiratory infections in Palangkaraya during the months-long crisis that has also affected Indonesia's neighbours with haze pollution.
The city's air quality index hit 4,000 this month, its worst ever measurement and more than 13 times the environment ministry's threshold for pollution deemed "hazardous" to health.
The World Health Organisation has linked exposure to air pollution, including high levels of tiny, airborne PM2.5 particles, to increased risk of illness and premature death.
Palangkaraya resident Muhammad Jihan Alwi used the reprieve to jog outdoors for the first time in months.
"Of course I'm happy to be out jogging again, breathing in fresh air that's better than yesterday, just feeling grateful," the 23-year-old said, smiling.
- NOT OVER YET -
However, the BMKG climatology agency said dry weather would continue to dominate for a while, with more wildfires possible.
The BNPB disaster agency has said it is operating 61 planes and helicopters for cloud seeding and water bombing in six Indonesian provinces.
Light to heavy rains have recently fallen in Central Kalimantan, South Kalimantan and South Sumatra, encouraged by its cloud seeding operations, said the agency.
"With the onset of rain, PM2.5 concentrations in Palangkaraya have also begun to show a decline," BMKG official Tri Handoko Seto told AFP on Thursday.
"Although still in the 'unhealthy' category, there is now a downward trend compared with a week ago, when levels were predominantly in the 'very unhealthy' and even 'hazardous' categories."
Tri said the short-term prediction was for rain clouds in affected provinces.
Efforts to seed them in a bid to stimulate more rain would continue "in the hope that the rain can truly soak the burned peat areas down to below the surface."
But he said vigilance was necessary "bearing in mind that there is still the possibility of another dry period before we fully enter the peak of the rainy season."
At least 11 people have died fighting Indonesia's wildfires, most recently a 45-year-old forest ranger who was killed by a falling tree while battling flames in North Toraja, South Sulawesi, on Wednesday.
Police said Thursday they were continuing to crack down on individuals and corporations responsible for the fires.
The national police's top detective, Asep Safrudin, said 245 individuals and 20 corporations have been named as suspects and could face jail time and heavy fines.
Deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas says the fires consumed more than 1.9 million hectares in the nine months to September.
The haze has sent pollution levels soaring as far afield as Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and East Timor, clouding Indonesia's ties with its neighbours.
Experts say the wildfires can be blamed in large part on slash-and-burn land-clearing practices, often by timber, palm oil or mining companies.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CSA to strengthen political stability, advance reforms, says Taufiq
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The
confidence and supply agreement
(CSA) between the Madani government and MPs from Bersatu, Muda and among independents will strengthen political stability and advance institutional reforms.
Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said the agreement reflected democratic maturity, with national interests taking precedence over political differences.
"It would also help ensure the smooth passage and implementation of the 2027 Budget, allowing the government to continue its economic development agenda and strengthen social protection," he said in a statement today.
He said the agreement would also support institutional reforms, including limiting the prime minister's tenure and separating the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor.
He commended Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's willingness to negotiate across political divides, saying such an approach could strengthen political stability.
"The time has come for Malaysia to move forward beyond political differences and disputes," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt discussing automatic screen-time limits for children with online platforms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is in talks with online platforms to introduce automatic screen-time limits for children, including mandatory breaks after prolonged use, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said discussions were also being held with his counterparts from several Asean countries on introducing the restrictions by default, without requiring parents to activate them manually.
"For example, children watching YouTube Shorts could be limited to one hour. After that, they would have to take a break.
"We hope all platforms with autoplay features can introduce screen-time limits so that children can take a break," he said when winding up the debate on the 2027 Supply Bill for his ministry.
Fahmi said the proposed limits could be adjusted according to users' needs but did not specify when the measure could be introduced or whether any agreement had been reached.
He said the RM58.7 million allocated for the Safe Internet Campaign under the 2027 Budget would also fund programmes to educate parents, guardians and teachers on protecting children from online threats.
He added that many parents were unaware that existing parental control features on electronic devices could be used to restrict their children's screen time.
On online gaming safety, he said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission and the Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia (CMCF) were studying emerging risks and appropriate safeguards.
He said MCMC was also examining international practices to identify effective safety measures, while CMCF was conducting public consultations to develop a gaming subcode.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Axis-Reit posts higher net profit of RM54.79mil in Q3
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Axis Real Estate Investment Trust (Reit) posted a higher net profit of RM54.79 million for third quarter (Q3) ended Sept 30, 2026, compared to RM52.12 million in the same period last year.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, it said revenue slid to RM90.77 million from RM92.76 million a year earlier.
For the nine-month period ended Sept 30, 2026, Axis-Reit said it chalked up a better net profit of RM154.30 million compared to RM148.20 million in the previous year's corresponding period, while revenue decreased to RM270.13 million from RM272.88 million previously.
"The realised net income generated from operations was RM144.41 million after deducting total expenditure of RM125.71 million, of which RM38.91 million was attributable to property expenses and RM86.80 million to non-property expenses," it said.
On prospects, the company said it remains optimistic about maintaining its current performance for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, supported by the satisfactory performance of its existing property portfolio and its strategy of actively pursuing quality investments.
Meanwhile, Axis-Reit Managers Bhd chief executive officer and executive director Leong Kit May said the third-quarter performance reflected its continued focus on proactive portfolio management to sustain income growth and strengthen resilience amid a changing operating environment.
"With an acquisition target of RM250 million, we will continue to pursue quality acquisition opportunities, while maintaining a strong focus on portfolio occupancy, tenant relationships and enhancing the performance of our existing properties," she said in a separate statement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sukuk dissolution event does not require immediate full repayment, says Zetrix AI
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI acknowledges that a dissolution event had been triggered under its Sukuk Wakalah Programme following a breach of a covenant requiring Wong Thean Soon to remain its single largest shareholder.
However, the event did not require it to repay the full outstanding amount immediately under the programme, Zetrix AI replied to a query from Bursa Malaysia today.
"The company will continue to engage with the sukuk trustee and sukukholders to resolve the outstanding matters in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Sukuk Wakalah Programme," it said.
Zetrix AI, formerly known as MyEG Services Bhd, collects payments for Malaysian government agencies and operates the Zetrix blockchain platform.
On Oct 16, it was reported that Zetrix AI Bhd faced a potential breach of a covenant under its RM2 billion Sukuk Wakalah programme after managing director Wong Thean Soon ceased to be the company's single largest shareholder following forced share sales by banks.
In the bourse reply, the company stated that it has made all payments due under the Sukuk Wakalah Programme in accordance with the stipulated payment schedule.
The company said it would make an immediate announcement pursuant to Paragraph 9.19A of the Main Market listing requirements of Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd should an event of default in payment occur.
The next sukuk holders' meeting date has not been fixed pending the availability of all parties, it added.
During the Oct 23 sukuk holders' meeting, no resolution was passed, but the existing terms and conditions of the Sukuk Wakalah Programme remain in force, it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelantan Wawasan membership nears 30,000 in just over three months
Article:
KUALA KRAI: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) has recorded nearly 30,000 new members across Kelantan in just over three months, reflecting growing membership in all 14 divisions in the state.
Kelantan Wawasan liaison deputy chairman Che Johan Che Pa said membership continued to increase daily, driven by sustained efforts by the party leadership and grassroots members.
"Wawasan in Kelantan managed to attract nearly 30,000 members within a short period despite being relatively new.
"This is a good sign for us," he said at a ceremony to hand over appointment letters to more than 10 members of the Kuala Krai Wawasan division committee during a Sembang Santai programme.
Among those who received the appointment letters were the Kuala Krai division secretary and its youth chief.
Also present were Kuala Krai Wawasan pro-tem division chief Tuan Mastura Tuan Ibrahim and several senior state party leaders.
Earlier in his speech, Che Johan said Kelantan Wawasan had attracted many new members, particularly among the younger generation.
He said the party would continue to strengthen youth participation as part of its efforts to expand its membership in the state.
"So far, we have seen an encouraging response from young people, and this development motivates us to further strengthen their involvement in the party," he said.
He said many political parties were established to compete against and challenge others, but Wawasan adopted a different approach by prioritising social unity and shared prosperity.
He said the party aspired to serve as a platform to unite people regardless of their backgrounds while ensuring that prosperity could be enjoyed collectively.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor DOE probes Sungai Kim Kim after river turns white again, cable excavation suspected
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 29 — The Johor Department of Environment (DOE) is investigating allegations that Sungai Kim Kim in Pasir Gudang has become polluted again, turning white yesterday.
Johor DOE director Dr Mohd Famey Yusoff said enforcement officers inspected the site at about 6pm following a complaint about the incident.
However, he said preliminary inspections yesterday found that the river water had returned to normal and was no longer visibly white.
Mohd Famey said preliminary investigations suggested that the incident could have been caused by a one-off waste discharge into the river.
“Nevertheless, the DOE, together with the Pasir Gudang City Council (MBPG), will examine closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage in the vicinity of the suspected dumping site,” he told Bernama.
Mohd Famey said the CCTV footage would be examined to identify the source of the pollution and those responsible.
He said strict legal action would be taken against any party or individual found to be involved in the waste dumping incident.
Yesterday, a social media post went viral alleging that Sungai Kim Kim had been polluted again, accompanied by several photographs showing the river water turning white.
The chemical pollution incident at Sungai Kim Kim in March 2019 shocked the nation, affecting more than 2,000 people and resulting in the closure of 111 schools in Pasir Gudang.
Meanwhile, State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said that the pollution was believed to have been caused by excavation work to a depth of about five metres for cable installation.
He said the information was based on further investigations conducted by the DOE today.
“The cable installation work was carried out yesterday at about 3pm,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Ling said the state government understood the public’s concerns and stressed that it took all reports involving environmental quality seriously, adding that it would ensure the relevant agencies carried out appropriate monitoring and follow-up action.
Members of the public are also encouraged to lodge complaints if they detect any suspicious activities or signs of environmental pollution, so that investigations and further action can be carried out promptly. — Bernama

Title: Govt increases allocations to all states, Sabah and Sarawak receive highest sums, says Amir Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The federal government has always prioritised projects proposed by the state governments, including increasing allocations to all states, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
He said that since 2023, several main grants have been enhanced, with the Economic, Infrastructure and Welfare Development-Based Grants (TAHAP Grants) increased to RM400 million per year.
Meanwhile, the allocation for the Malaysian Road Records Information System (MARRIS) increased to RM5.6 billion in 2026 from RM5.2 billion in 2023.
“The allocation for the Ecological Fiscal Transfer (EFT) increased to RM270 million in the 2027 Budget from RM150 million in 2023. This increase supports services, infrastructure, and environmental preservation in the states,” he said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage for the Ministry of Finance (MoF) in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said the Madani government also increased Sabah’s interim special grant from RM26.7 million in 2021 to RM1.5 billion, which is more than 50 times. For Sarawak, the interim special grant increased from RM16 million in 2022 to RM1.5 billion, which is more than 90 times.
Meanwhile, Amir Hamzah said the overall allocation for Sabah and Sarawak is the highest, increasing to RM18.7 billion and RM16.2 billion, respectively.
Sabah’s RM18.7 billion allocation comprises RM8.9 billion for operating expenses, RM7 billion for development, and RM2.8 billion in grants to the state government.
He said the government respects the principle of special grants in line with the Constitution, and negotiations are ongoing to finalise a fair and sustainable method of calculation.
“This is the commitment of the Madani Government to drive the development of Sabah and Sarawak while negotiations are underway,” he said.
Federal expenditures are projected to rise from a revised estimate of RM444.1 billion in 2026 to RM459.8 billion in 2027, of which RM376.8 billion will be operating expenditure and RM83 billion as development expenditure. — Bernama

Title: MCA gets Bandar Hilir as third Melaka seat to contest, says Wee Ka Siong
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong said the party has been given an additional seat - Bandar Hilir - to contest in the Melaka State Election.
He said Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) finalised the decision today, with MCA set to contest in three state constituencies, including Machap Jaya and Kelebang.
Wee said its candidate for the Bandar Hilir state seat will be Melaka Historic City Council councillor Jasmine Lok Huey Yee, 38.
“Officially, MCA will contest the two seats that we won in 2021, namely Machap Jaya and Kelebang, and now we have been given an additional seat in Bandar Hilir.
“BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi handed over the letters of appointment for candidates at 4pm today,” he told a media conference at the Parliament Building today.
Wee said the additional seat was part of the process of finalising seat allocations between BN and PN for the Melaka polls.
He said this follows key PN leaders’ willingness to allocate the seat in question to MCA, which had contested the constituency previously, adding that the move would not affect the strategic cooperation between BN and its strategic partners for the state election.
“... (we) received a call from key PN leaders expressing their willingness to allow MCA to contest, as this is a seat we had contested in the past,” he said.
Overall, BN will contest 22 seats at the 16th Melaka polls.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as the polling day for the Melaka state election, with nomination day scheduled for Saturday (October 31) and early voting for November 10. — Bernama

Title: MACC issues asset declaration notices to businessman Nazir Hussin and brother
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) issued asset declaration notices to businessman Datuk Seri Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin and his brother, Datuk Mubarak Hussain, on October 20.
Nazir Hussin was at the MACC Office in Putrajaya to receive the notice under Section 36(1)(a) of the MACC Act 2009, while Mubarak Hussain received the notice at his residence.
When contacted, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the matter, saying both individuals complied with the notices.
On October 14, the MACC summoned Nazir Hussin, his wife and an aide to assist in an investigation into alleged misappropriation and abuse of position involving an investment deal worth about RM10 million.
The MACC said it summoned the former Yayasan Bank Rakyat (YBR) chairman to receive a notice requiring him to declare his assets, while his wife and the aide were summoned to record their statements.
Abd Halim was reported to have said that Nazir Hussin refused to accept the notice, citing an injunction application he had filed at the Kuala Lumpur High Court yesterday to stop enforcement of the directive issued under Section 36 of the Act. — Bernama

Title: Finance minister II: GST not an option amid high cost of living, govt sticking with SST
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The federal government will continue to implement the Sales and Service Tax (SST), as the Goods and Services Tax (GST) will not be considered due to the ongoing burden of the cost of living.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the government would continue to improve the SST to reduce the impact of cascading taxes and simplify compliance.
He said the SST also provided room for a more progressive and targeted approach.
“The government can choose which goods and services to tax while exempting essential items. Although some of the tax may be passed on through prices, the scope of taxation can be determined with the people’s affordability in mind,” said Amir Hamzah during the Supply Bill (Budget 2027) policy-level winding-up debate for the Ministry of Finance (MoF) in Parliament today.
He explained that the GST tended to be regressive because lower-income groups spent a larger proportion of their income on goods and services.
“In other words, even at the same tax rate, the burden relative to income is heavier for the people, particularly the B40 and M40 groups.
“Therefore, any additional revenue must be assessed alongside the burden borne by the people,” he said.
According to the Fiscal Outlook 2027, SST collections are estimated to rise to RM67 billion in 2026 from RM55.9 billion in 2025. They are projected to reach RM73.3 billion in 2027, an increase of RM17.4 billion over two years.
Amir Hamzah said SST collections currently account for three per cent of gross domestic product (GDP), the same level recorded by the GST in 2017.
This means replacing the SST with the GST would not necessarily generate additional revenue, but would instead shift the tax burden entirely from businesses, including exporters, to the people, he emphasised.
“This increase demonstrates the SST’s ability to generate revenue to finance the country’s needs.
“At the same time, the government has the flexibility to determine which goods and services are taxed on a targeted basis while exempting essential items,” said Amir Hamzah.
He said the government recognised GST’s advantages in collection efficiency, transparency and the input tax credit mechanism. However, the choice of tax system must take into account the people’s ability to pay.
On compliance, he said nearly 700,000 businesses were registered under the GST in 2018, compared with only about 130,000 under the SST in 2026. This means more businesses would have to bear compliance costs under the GST system, said Amir Hamzah. — Bernama

Title: MOH to conduct special recruitment for 750 permanent medical officer posts in Sabah, Sarawak
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 29 — The Health Ministry (MOH) will conduct a special recruitment exercise to fill 750 permanent Medical Officer Grade UD10 vacancies in Sabah and Sarawak, with applications open from November 9 to 15.
MOH said the recruitment is open to all contract-appointed medical officers who began their housemanship training from Series 1/2016 on December 5, 2016, to Series 6/2024 on October 14, 2024, including those whose service contracts had expired.
“To be eligible, candidates must have successfully completed their housemanship training and obtained full registration with the Malaysian Medical Council by the closing date of the application advertisement at the latest,” MOH said in a statement today.
The ministry said eligible and interested officers could submit their applications through the Public Service Commission’s SPA9 system when the recruitment advertisement opened.
“For officers who are successful in securing permanent appointments, the proposed reporting date is February 15, 2027,” the statement said.
The ministry said the recruitment exercise was part of the Madani Government’s commitment to making permanent appointments for more than 9,000 medical officers, as announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling Budget 2027.
“This proactive measure is also designed to narrow the staffing gap and ensure that the retention of the medical workforce in Sabah and Sarawak remains at an optimal level,” the statement said. — Bernama

Title: Former Pahang water firm procurement manager begins three-year jail term after losing bribery appeal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 29 — The Court of Appeal today upheld the three-year jail sentence and RM239,500 fine imposed on a former procurement manager of Pengurusan Air Pahang Berhad after dismissing his appeal to set aside his conviction on 22 charges of receiving RM44,700 in bribes.
A three-member panel led by Justice Datuk Noorin Badaruddin ruled that Sani Khan Ali Khan had failed to show any error of law or material fact in the High Court decision that convicted him on all the charges.
On January 26, the Kuantan High Court set aside a Sessions Court decision that had acquitted and discharged him of all the charges.
The Court of Appeal panel, which also comprised Justices Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, ordered him to begin serving his sentence today.
Sani Khan, 51, had previously been granted a stay of execution and released on RM20,000 bail with one surety pending the outcome of this appeal.
In today’s proceedings, Justice Noorin said the High Court’s intervention was justified and that it had made no material error in setting aside the Sessions Court decision that had acquitted and discharged Sani Khan.
“The statutory presumption under Section 50(1) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009 applies,” she said.
She said banking records proved that the money had been received into the appellant’s bank account, and that his claim that the payments were house rental was unconvincing.
Justice Noorin said that although the appellant relied on tenancy agreements and bank transactions labelled as house rent, the court found that the documents did not prove the payments were genuine rent.
She added that the appellant had also failed to show that the alleged defects in the charges had caused him to misunderstand the case or suffer material prejudice in preparing his defence.
Justice Noorin said the evidence was assessed cumulatively, with the banking records, witness testimony, tenancy documents and surrounding circumstances weighed together for each charge. The court found no material error warranting the overturning of any of the 22 convictions.
On December 26, 2024, the Sessions Court ruled that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt, and acquitted and discharged Sani Khan on all the charges.
However, the High Court allowed the prosecution’s appeal to set aside his acquittal and found him guilty on all 22 charges.
The High Court imposed three years’ jail for each charge and ordered Sani Khan to pay a RM239,500 fine, or 12 months’ jail in default. The sentences were ordered to run concurrently.
At the Court of Appeal today, MACC deputy public prosecutors Law Chin How, Haresh Prakash Somiah and Hazel Tan Jia Qi appeared for the prosecution.
Sani Khan was represented by lawyers Mohd Baharuddin Ahmad Kassim, Datuk Mohd Najid Husain and Nornajihah Ahmad Nadjemudin. — Bernama

Title: Menara Tun Perak, formerly Menara Maybank, on offer for full or partial sale
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Menara Tun Perak, the iconic Kuala Lumpur skyscraper formerly known as Menara Maybank, has reportedly been put up for sale after serving as the banking giant’s headquarters for nearly four decades.
According to a sponsored announcement published by property news website
Mingtiandi
, investors are being offered the opportunity to acquire either a partial or full interest in the building, although no asking price was disclosed.
Standing 244 metres tall along Jalan Tun Perak, the building was completed in 1988 and remains one of the capital’s most recognisable landmarks.
The proposed sale comes months after Maybank relocated its headquarters to Merdeka 118 on May 6, ending its longstanding use of the tower as its head office.
On July 28, Maybank announced that its new headquarters would be renamed Menara Merdeka Maybank, while its former headquarters would take the name Menara Tun Perak.
Property consultancy firms Knight Frank Malaysia and CBRE|WTW have reportedly been jointly appointed to advise on the proposed sale.
The building’s location near Chinatown, Central Market, Dataran Merdeka and several public transport stations is being promoted as a key attraction for potential investors.
According to the announcement, interested buyers could retain the property for commercial use, upgrade the existing building or explore converting it into a hotel, serviced accommodation or mixed-use development, subject to feasibility studies and regulatory approvals.
Knight Frank Malaysia head of capital markets James Buckley said properties of such prominence in Kuala Lumpur's historic commercial district were seldom offered to investors.
“Landmark assets of this nature, particularly those located within the city’s historic core, are rarely made available for investment,” he said.
CBRE|WTW director Marcus Yeo said the building's location and potential for alternative uses could appeal to investors amid the continued redevelopment of Kuala Lumpur's city centre.

Title: Muhyiddin: CSA has nothing to do with possible Bersatu-PH pact for Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) signed with the federal government today has nothing to do with a possible electoral pact with Pakatan Harapan (PH) for the Melaka polls,
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT) reported.
“That is a separate question. That has nothing to do with (the agreement) here,” he was quoted as telling reporters after the signing at Parliament.
According to the news portal, Muhyiddin was responding to a question on whether Bersatu would now form an electoral pact with PH in Melaka.
FMT reported that speculation of a tie-up emerged after leaders from both sides attended a closed-door dinner in Melaka on September 28, though the matter has faced pushback within PH.
Muhyiddin also said the CSA was separate from a similar agreement being sought between Bersatu and the PH-led Selangor government, the report said.
“That is another matter. This agreement is between the federal government, represented by the prime minister, and MPs representing my party and the other parties involved,” he said.
According to FMT, the CSA involved six Bersatu MPs and Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman. The MPs are seeking a limit on the prime minister’s tenure and the separation of the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor before the end of the government’s term.
They also want the same constituency development allocations that government backbenchers currently receive.
In return, the seven opposition MPs will support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s administration until the end of the parliamentary term, as well as Budget 2027, the news portal reported.
The six Bersatu MPs who signed are Muhyiddin (Pagoh), Datuk Radzi Jidin (Putrajaya), Ali Biju (Saratok), Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (Langkawi), Nazri Abu Hassan (Merbok) and Azman Nasrudin (Padang Serai).
FMT reported that six former Bersatu MPs, who were sacked in 2024 for declaring support for the government, also signed the deal. Muhyiddin said their signing was merely a formality as they had already expressed support for the prime minister.
He said Bersatu would remain in the opposition and continue to provide checks and balances despite the agreement.
Muhyiddin added that the CSA is expected to remain in force until Parliament is dissolved, but could be terminated if either side failed to honour its commitments.
Separately, Syed Saddiq told FMT the CSA must lead to legislation guaranteeing fair and equal constituency allocations for all MPs, rather than benefiting only those who signed it.
He said the agreement specified that allocations for MPs on both sides must be equal, although the exact amounts had not been disclosed.

Title: Kedah police arrest man over viral video of reckless driving in ‘Bomba’ MPV
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 29 — Police have arrested a 35-year-old man over a viral video showing him allegedly driving recklessly in a red multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) bearing the word ‘Bomba’.
Kuala Muda police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said investigations found that the man had been diagnosed with bipolar disorder nine years ago but was believed to have discontinued treatment about two years ago.
“Police received a report on Tuesday following the video’s circulation. The man was arrested in Bandar Puteri Jaya, where the vehicle and several other items were seized,” he told reporters at the Kuala Muda district police headquarters here today.
Hanyan said the man owned the MPV, held a valid driving licence and had no previous criminal record. His urine screening test was negative.
The case is being investigated under Section 170 of the Penal Code for impersonating a public servant and Section 42 of the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless and dangerous driving.
The man was remanded for one day before being admitted to Sungai Petani Hospital for treatment and further monitoring.
Hanyan urged families to ensure members with a history of psychiatric treatment attend scheduled follow-up appointments.
The viral video showed the man driving recklessly in the red MPV marked ‘Bomba’ and berating motorists who did not give way to him. — Bernama

Title: Transport minister takes first AirBorneo flight, stresses need for reliable air links to remote communities
Article:
MIRI, Oct 29 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke took his first flight with AirBorneo on a trip from Miri to Limbang, highlighting the importance of rural air connectivity for communities in Sarawak and Sabah.
In a Facebook post on Wednesday, Loke shared photographs of himself on the tarmac with one of the airline’s turboprop aircraft before travelling to Limbang to officiate a local government function.
“Reliable air connectivity is an absolute lifeline for communities in the interior of Sarawak and Sabah.
“Seeing AirBorneo successfully operate these essential routes reinforces our shared commitment to leaving no community isolated,” he said in the post.
Loke said the ministry would continue to support the development of regional aviation to ensure rural communities remained accessible.
AirBorneo operates the Rural Air Services (RAS) in Sarawak and Sabah, connecting remote settlements such as Bario and Long Lellang, where road access is limited or unavailable.
These flights provide an essential transport link for residents, particularly in medical emergencies and for the delivery of essential goods.
The airline’s fleet includes ATR 72 turboprop aircraft serving main routes linking Miri, Kuching and Kota Kinabalu, as well as DHC-6 Twin Otters designed for short take-off and landing at remote airstrips that cannot accommodate larger aircraft.
Beyond its Rural Air Services, AirBorneo also operates scheduled domestic and international passenger flights.
